idiom_name: hand-written gate over Thread::Mutex + Thread::ConditionVariable, or Concurrent::ReadWriteLock from concurrent-ruby
implementation_notes: Ruby's stdlib lock types are exclusive: Thread::Mutex, Monitor/MonitorMixin and Thread::ConditionVariable; there is no reader-writer lock, so the gate is written with a mutex, a condition variable, a reader count and a writer flag. Adopt concurrent-ruby's Concurrent::ReadWriteLock (with_read_lock/with_write_lock, write-preferring, non-reentrant, explicitly modelled on java.util.concurrent.ReentrantReadWriteLock) when a gem dependency is acceptable; hand-roll only to avoid it. The lock is justified where MRI releases the GVL during read sections (I/O-bound readers); with CPU-bound Ruby the GVL serialises threads anyway, and Ractors cannot share the mutable object at all, so message passing is the alternative there.
pitfalls: Concurrent::ReadWriteLock forbids upgrade and re-entry: taking the write lock while holding a read lock (or taking it twice) deadlocks.
The MRI GVL means threads do not run CPU-bound Ruby in parallel, so the lock buys throughput only when read sections release the GVL (I/O); otherwise it is pure overhead.
Ractor isolation forbids sharing mutable objects between Ractors - a lock cannot fix that; pass messages or freeze the data.
A hand-rolled gate must release in ensure (as with_read_lock/with_write_lock do); a missed exception path leaves the lock held forever.
